decisionsTaken: Focus policy for non-modal popovers (left open by the spike): focus moves to the first focusable element of the content, or to the panel; Tab order follows the trigger; focus leaving closes it.
label required: the panel is a named non-modal dialog.
Surface color.surface.overlay, shadow.overlay, elevation border, radius.overlay, padding space.content.md, max inline size size.overlay.panel (new semantic role, 360 px), offset space.content.xs.
Side bottom or top, align start by default; flips, shifts and follows the trigger on scroll.
No built-in close button: content adds one when it needs it (Escape and a press outside always close).
nextAction: Wave 4 changes accepted with the wave 4 implementation gate; the Figma master was re-checked at the wave 4 Figma parity (unchanged); the documentation is re-checked with the wave 4 documentation step.
implementationNotes: The trigger is rendered by a snippet that spreads popovertarget and the popup attributes on a Button or IconButton: the browser toggles the auto popover, which spares the trigger from light dismiss (no close-then-reopen on the same press) and restores focus to it on Escape.
On opening, the panel's max block size is the larger room above or below the trigger, so that it flips and scrolls instead of overflowing the viewport.
